original_question: For H_n = {(x,y) in Z x Z : xy congruent to 1 mod n and 1 <= x,y <= n-1}, let v(n) be the number of vertices of the convex hull of H_n. Is v(n) forced to tend to infinity with n, and can one sharpen the lower-density estimate for the error term D(n) = v(n) - 2(tau(n-1)-1) on the set where D(n)=0?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper’s introductory problem package consisting of Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 for the modular-inversion point set G_n (your H_n), namely: whether the number v(n) of vertices of the convex hull tends to infinity; the divisor-forced lower bound v(n) >= 2(τ(n-1)-1); and the positive lower-density result for the equality case D(n)=0. The arXiv identifier supplied in the prompt, 1406.3558, is unrelated; the matching paper is arXiv:0711.4100.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct object (the modular-inversion lattice points with xy ≡ 1 mod n), the correct statistic v(n) (vertices of the convex hull), the correct normalization D(n)=v(n)-2(τ(n-1)-1), and the two paper-faithful directions suggested by the introduction: (i) whether v(n) must grow without bound, and (ii) whether the paper’s lower-density estimate for the equality case D(n)=0 can be improved. Using H_n instead of the paper’s G_n is only a notational change.
missing_details: The paper defines the convex body explicitly as the convex hull C_n = conv(G_n) (or conv(H_n)) inside R^2; v(n) counts vertices of this planar convex polygon, not just extremal points in an abstract combinatorial sense.
The paper’s notation for the point set is G_n rather than H_n.
τ(n-1) should be identified explicitly as the divisor-counting function.
The role of Proposition 1.2 should be built into the question: D(n) is introduced precisely because Proposition 1.2 gives v(n) >= 2(τ(n-1)-1).
The set whose density is being discussed should be stated explicitly as {n >= 2 : D(n)=0} = {n >= 2 : v(n)=2(τ(n-1)-1)}.
The density in Theorem 1.3 is a lower asymptotic density, so 'lower-density estimate' should be spelled out as a bound on lim inf_{x->infinity} x^{-1} #{n <= x : D(n)=0}.
The growth question should use the exact asymptotic quantifier 'as n -> infinity'.
To stay paper-faithful, the refined question should reference the equality case singled out by Theorem 1.3, not a broader distribution problem for D(n).
refined_question: Let G_n = {(x,y) in Z^2 : xy ≡ 1 (mod n), 1 <= x,y <= n-1}, let C_n = conv(G_n) ⊂ R^2, and let v(n) be the number of vertices of C_n. Since Proposition 1.2 gives v(n) >= 2(τ(n-1)-1), define D(n) = v(n) - 2(τ(n-1)-1). Is it true that v(n) -> infinity as n -> infinity, and can the explicit lower bound in Theorem 1.3 for the lower asymptotic density of the equality set {n >= 2 : D(n)=0} = {n >= 2 : v(n)=2(τ(n-1)-1)} be improved?
justification: The supplied draft matches the modular-inversions paper, not arXiv:1406.3558. The identifier 1406.3558 is a CANT problem-session compilation with a different title and scope, whereas arXiv:0711.4100 has exactly the defining set of modular inverses in the square [1,n-1]^2 and studies the number of vertices of its convex hull. Within that paper, the introduction organizes the topic around Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3, and your draft is best read as combining those three introductory items into one stand-alone question. The draft is already very close, but to be fully self-contained and paper-faithful it should explicitly name the convex hull, the divisor function τ, the lower-bound origin of D(n), and the precise lower-density set appearing in Theorem 1.3.
